  • • The impact-sensitive chemical mixture in a cartridge primer — 1 mark

questions.question: What is the Walker test? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the Walker test? (2 marks)
  • • A chemical test historically used to detect nitrite residues around a bullet hole — 1 mark
  • • May help estimate firing distance; it is presumptive and must be interpreted with controls/limitations — 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the forensic significance of bullet striations. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the forensic significance of bullet striations. (2 marks)
  • • Striations are microscopic marks imparted by the barrel during passage — 1 mark
  • • Their pattern can support comparison of a questioned bullet with test bullets from a suspected firearm — 1 mark

questions.question: A bullet loses its gyroscopic stability during flight. What effect would this have on its motion. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• A bullet loses its gyroscopic stability during flight. What effect would this have on its motion? (2 marks)
  • • The bullet may yaw or tumble rather than remain point-forward — 1 mark
  • • This can increase drag and reduce accuracy/range, and may affect impact behaviour — 1 mark

questions.question: Differentiate between muzzle flash and muzzle blast. / [CO3] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between muzzle flash and muzzle blast. (2 marks)
  • • Muzzle flash: visible light from hot gases/combustion products at the muzzle — 1 mark
  • • Muzzle blast: pressure wave/noise caused by rapidly expanding gases — 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the role of propellants in ammunition and mention their important characteristics. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of propellants in ammunition and mention their important characteristics. (4 marks)
  • • Generate hot gases on combustion to propel the projectile — 1 mark
  • • Controlled, rapid gas generation and suitable pressure curve — 1 mark
  • • Characteristics: chemical stability and predictable burning rate — 1 mark
  • • Adequate energy with manageable residue/corrosion and safe storage; any valid point — 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the role of the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) in linking firearm-related incidents. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) in linking firearm-related
  • incidents. (4 marks)
  • • Digital system/database for ballistic evidence, especially cartridge-case images — 1 mark
  • • Captures and compares characteristic breech-face/firing-pin and other marks — 1 mark
  • • Generates investigative leads linking shootings or evidence items — 1 mark
  • • Candidate associations require confirmation by trained examiner; database result alone is not final identification — 1 mark

questions.question: Describe the important identifying features of a 12-bore firearm and a .315 firearm. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the important identifying features of a 12-bore firearm and a .315 firearm. (4 marks)
  • • 12-bore: shotgun gauge designation; commonly smoothbore and fires shotshells, though configurations vary — 1 mark
  • • 12-bore cartridge/chamber and barrel features; record make, markings, serial number and action — 1 mark
  • • .315: commonly a rifle chambered for .315-inch-class ammunition in Indian usage; typically rifled barrel — 1 mark
  • • Document calibre/chamber markings, rifling, action, serial/maker marks and condition; do not rely on calibre label alone —
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe how the range of firing for a shotgun can be determined. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how the range of firing for a shotgun can be determined. (4 marks)
  • • Examine wound/target and distribution of pellets, wad and residue — 1 mark
  • • Conduct controlled test-fires using the same firearm/ammunition at known distances — 1 mark
  • • Compare pellet spread, wad impacts and GSR/soot patterns with questioned evidence — 1 mark
  • • Account for ammunition, barrel/choke, target, intervening material and environmental variation; estimate range rather than
  • claim exact distance — 1 mark
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the Price test and its significance in firearm examination. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the Price test and its significance in firearm examination. (4 marks)
  • • A presumptive chemical test associated with detecting lead residues around a suspected bullet hole — 1 mark
  • • Reagent reaction/colour change is interpreted according to the prescribed method and controls — 1 mark
  • • May assist in locating/assessing bullet holes or residue patterns — 1 mark
  • • Not conclusive alone; possible false results and need for confirmatory/alternative examination — 1 mark
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define intermediate ballistics and explain its importance in the study of firearm projectile motion. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define intermediate ballistics and explain its importance in the study of firearm projectile motion. (4 marks)
  • • Study of projectile behaviour as it exits the muzzle and interacts with gases near the firearm — 1 mark
  • • Covers transition from internal to external ballistics — 1 mark
  • • Includes muzzle blast/flash, gas effects and projectile disturbance near muzzle — 1 mark
  • • Helps understand stability, accuracy, trajectory and firing effects — 1 mark

questions.question: Describe the magazine and firing mechanism of a firearm and explain their functions / [CO1] [4x5 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the magazine and firing mechanism of a firearm and explain their functions. (4 marks)
  • • Magazine stores and feeds cartridges into the firearm — 1 mark
  • • May be detachable or integral; spring/follower commonly assist feeding — 1 mark
  • • Firing mechanism includes trigger, sear and hammer/striker components — 1 mark
  • • Trigger releases the mechanism to strike the primer; safe handling and design vary by firearm — 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the significance of GSR composition, positioning and collection in establishing a connection between a person and a firearm incident. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the significance of GSR composition, positioning and collection in establishing a connection between a person
  • and a firearm incident. (10 marks)
  • • Define gunshot residue (GSR) and explain that it may contain primer/propellant and projectile-related particles — 2 marks
  • • Composition: characteristic inorganic/organic constituents and the importance of validated analytical methods — 2 marks
  • • Positioning: hands, clothing and nearby surfaces; distribution depends on distance, firearm, ammunition and activity — 2
  • marks
  • • Collection: timely collection, suitable validated kits, separate samples, contamination prevention, controls and chain of
  • custody — 2 marks
  • • Interpretation: GSR supports an association but does not by itself prove firing; transfer, persistence, background and absence
  • limitations — 2 marks
